workloads.consumer: inference per-worker IO completion and rendering upload owner
workloads.task: Keep one suspending typed task on each of four worker-owned rings across repeated foreign completion wakes, then join every result.
workloads.lifecycle: Scheduler and four worker-owned tasks are persistent; 256 warmup episodes precede 4096 measured episodes; every task publishes one fresh Waker, suspends, resumes on its owner, acknowledges completion, returns a checksum and is joined.
workloads.semantic_equivalence: The candidate uses spawn_task_on plus JoinHandle. The migration baseline uses only the pre-v6 public Task, spawn_detached_on, one caller-owned typed result slot and one WaitGroup per task. Both charge the same publication, foreign wake, pinned reinjection/resume, typed completion and per-task join; construction is setup for the long-lived owner lifecycle.
workloads.negative_space: This is not an unpinned load-balancing row, a detached fire-and-forget row, a worker-stack callback, an empty task or an IO/backend latency benchmark.
